long_biography.plain_text:
A Manhattan townhouse redevelopment gave Scott Wilpon a direct role in Sterling Equities' property business. He oversaw its renovation, while a separate Queens housing venture listed him among the principals of a Sterling development entity. Sterling was established by his uncle Fred Wilpon and Saul Katz; Scott joined the family's real-estate investment firm as a partner.

His work extended into gaming and media. He helped establish the venture-capital arm Sterling.VC and the New York esports organisation NYXL, drawing on the family's existing sports and media interests. He also held a SportsNet New York role tied to its Mets partnership. After the Katz and Wilpon families divided most of Sterling's assets, Wilpon left the firm with Fred and Richard to pursue separate ventures. The two groups kept a shared interest in a property-development business.
